digest.definition: A primary healthcare profession that diagnoses, manages, treats and prevents a range of disorders, and an Allied Health Profession in England
distinctiveFeatures: A primary healthcare profession that diagnoses, manages, treats and prevents a range of disorders, and an Allied Health Profession in England
Care centres on the person, not the condition, and supports the body's own capacity to keep and restore health, with biopsychosocial factors always in view

Its methods combine person-centred tools, hands-on technique, palpation, rehabilitation exercise and self-help advice, with diagnosis built from case history and examination and guided by clinical reasoning
It is a regulated profession: only those registered with the General Osteopathic Council may practise or use the title, and graduates may practise autonomously from registration
Training joins academic study with extensive supervised clinical work in teaching clinics, at least 1,000 hours
It is evidence-informed and self-critical, weighing research, clinical experience and patient expectations and appraising its own claims (D1, 1.9, 6.6, 3.6 d) iv, 3.6 m) iii).
Most osteopaths are self-employed, so business, enterprise and practice management sit inside the curriculum (D1, 1.7, 1.26 to 1.39, 3.6 n)).

themesInSubject.inThisSubject: framed as a collective responsibility of an inclusive learning community that reaches past legal minimums: critical theory and decolonial perspectives across the curriculum, anticipatory design for each learning site (technique class, clinic, online), care for self and others and questions for reviewing a course; in practice, attention to protected characteristics, socioeconomic status and diverse patient groups (D1, 1.13 to 1.19, 3.6 e) vi, 4.4, 6.10)

part-time and full-time modes, blended and recorded delivery and reasonable adjustments, always bounded by the regulation that protects patient safety in clinic (D1, 1.20 to 1.22); accessible communication with digital tools (D1, 1.33)

whole-person training, critical study of the profession's structures and discourses, the eight UNESCO competencies modelled in facilities and curricula and personal and social responsibility for well-being (D1, 1.23 to 1.25); sustainable delivery of teaching (D1, 4.2)

named employability, enterprise and entrepreneurship education (EEE): most osteopaths are self-employed, so the entrepreneurial mindset, career planning, marketing, legal and financial skills, external speakers and clinic placements prepare graduates for private practice (D1, 1.26 to 1.39); a viable business that puts patients before profit (D1, 3.6 n) v)

subjectSpecific.text: You will be a competent practitioner with strong hands-on and manual therapy skills, able to solve problems using a range of approaches for different patients.
You will have the knowledge and clinical ability to bring many factors together and look at a patient's health needs as a whole.
You will be caring, empathetic and trustworthy, and work with patients as partners.
You will act with the attitudes, values and behaviour expected of a health professional, including on consent, safeguarding and honesty when things go wrong.
You will value what osteopathy can do for patients of all ages and know where its limits lie, especially the limits of your own knowledge and skill.

transferable.text: You will be reflective, self-aware and curious, and committed to learning throughout your career.

Purposes and characteristics of an Osteopathy degree

statements.appliesTo: anyone seeking to practise as an osteopath in the UK
statements.about: registration, Recognised Qualifications and the OPS
statements.paraphrase: Osteopathy courses are extended and mix academic with hands-on clinical work; the General Osteopathic Council regulates the profession and by law only its registrants may use the title or practise; anyone who trains here as an osteopath must gain a qualification the regulator recognises and the Privy Council approves; every Recognised Qualification must deliver the Osteopathic Practice Standards and should align with the regulator's guidance on graduate outcomes; the Professional Standards Authority oversees the regulator.

forPractitioner.text: Courses that lead to registration must hold Recognised Qualification status from the GOsC with Privy Council approval, must deliver the Osteopathic Practice Standards and should align with the regulator's guidance, including its graduate outcomes and education standards.

forBeneficiary.text: If you want to practise as an osteopath in the UK, you must gain a qualification recognised by the professional regulator, because by law only registered osteopaths may use the title or practise.

headingPath: Context and purposes of an Osteopathy degree
Purposes and characteristics of an Osteopathy degree

statements.appliesTo: students on pre-registration courses
statements.about: readiness for autonomous practice at graduation
statements.paraphrase: Once qualified and registered, osteopaths may practise on their own, so pre-registration education must ready them for autonomous practice by graduation; this requires them to develop the skills and criticality to join the osteopathic and wider health community and care well for patients, and the reflexivity and insight to keep abreast of evidence and stay fit to practise.

forPractitioner.text: Because registered osteopaths may practise independently, the course must prepare students for autonomous practice by graduation: the skills and criticality to work within the osteopathic and wider health community, and the reflexivity to keep abreast of evidence and remain fit to practise.

forBeneficiary.text: Because you may work on your own as soon as you register, your course must prepare you for independent practice by the time you graduate: you will need the skills and critical thinking to work with other health professionals, and the habit of keeping up with evidence and staying fit to practise.

headingPath: Context and purposes of an Osteopathy degree

statements.appliesTo: osteopathic practice and its teaching
statements.about: care centred on the person, not the condition
statements.paraphrase: Focusing on the person rather than the condition is a long-held principle of osteopathy and should shape the osteopathic approach to care; it means seeing the person as a combined mix of influences that together affect health.

forPractitioner.text: Teach and model care that centres on the person rather than the condition: this long-held tenet should shape the approach to care, treating health as the product of many interacting influences.

forBeneficiary.text: You should centre your care on the person, not just their condition, seeing their health as the result of many influences working together.

headingPath: Context and purposes of an Osteopathy degree

statements.appliesTo: everyone in the osteopathic learning community
statements.about: shared responsibility for equity and inclusion
statements.paraphrase: The osteopathic learning community holds a shared responsibility, going past the legal minimum, to build equity, equality, diversity and inclusion into institutions, processes, curricula and teaching, for example by widening participation, countering under-representation, refusing all discrimination and harassment, securing access for neurodiverse members and closing awarding gaps; everyone in it will need to engage, reflect and change to meet this duty.

forPractitioner.text: Embed equity, equality, diversity and inclusion across institutions, processes, curricula and pedagogy as a collective responsibility that goes past legal minimums: widen participation, counter under-representation, tolerate no discrimination or microaggression, secure access for neurodiverse members and close awarding gaps; all participants will need to engage, reflect and change.

forBeneficiary.text: You, like everyone in the osteopathic community, will be expected to engage, reflect and be open to change so that learning is fair and inclusive for all.

headingPath: Context and purposes of an Osteopathy degree

statements.appliesTo: everyone involved in osteopathy and its learning community
statements.about: an inclusive community that counters systemic disadvantage
statements.paraphrase: Everyone in osteopathy should build an inclusive learning community of students, staff, patients, visitors and partners that works against systemic disadvantage; inclusion needs strong commitment and joint action so that all can reach their potential free of harassment, prejudice or discrimination; present-day legacies such as racism, classism, ableism, homophobia and patriarchy must be acknowledged and countered, for instance through varied teaching methods.

forPractitioner.text: Foster an inclusive community of students, academics, professional staff, patients, visitors and partners; act with commitment so all can reach their potential without harassment or discrimination; acknowledge and counter the legacies of systemic disadvantage, for example with diverse teaching methods. The countering is a must; the fostering a should.

forBeneficiary.text: You should help build a learning community where everyone, patients and visitors included, belongs, and where racism, ableism, homophobia and other prejudice must be named and challenged.

headingPath: Context and purposes of an Osteopathy degree

statements.appliesTo: undergraduate and postgraduate osteopathic study
statements.paraphrase: Osteopathic study at every level should keep questioning critically the language, perceptions and entrenched dominant systems of thought within ideas of knowledge and power; social justice rests on agency, equal rights and human dignity, and equity is treated as an ethical matter and a basic right that supports anti-oppressive knowledge and practice.

forPractitioner.text: Build continual critical interrogation of the discipline's language, perceptions and dominant systems of thought into undergraduate and postgraduate study, framing equity as an ethical matter and a human right that supports anti-oppressive knowledge and practice.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on courses in shaping the curriculum; the student meets its effect

headingPath: Context and purposes of an Osteopathy degree

statements.appliesTo: the osteopathy curriculum
statements.paraphrase: An ethics of care, valuing plural knowledges and experiences, respect for different perspectives and lifestyles, attention to decolonial imperatives and solidarity against injustice underpin the inclusive community; these values should run through the whole curriculum rather than sit in single modules, helping students engage with health inequalities and varied patient groups.

forPractitioner.text: Integrate the community's core values (an ethics of care, plural knowledges, respect, decolonial attention and solidarity) across the curriculum, not in isolated modules, so that students engage with health inequalities, social determinants and diverse patients.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on course design; the student meets its effect in the curriculum

headingPath: Context and purposes of an Osteopathy degree

statements.appliesTo: the osteopathy curriculum and its design
statements.paraphrase: The core values support curriculum design that encourages critical thinking drawn from progressive theories and educational research, drawing on critical and critical race theory, decolonial thought, disability, feminist and queer studies and the study of science and technology; critical theory should be applied across the discipline and its content, and the values also favour anticipatory design suited to each site of learning, with care for those that have been less inclusive.

forPractitioner.text: Apply critical theory across the discipline and curriculum (critical race theory, decoloniality, disability, feminist, queer and science and technology studies among others) and design anticipatorily for each learning site, whether online, face to face, technique class or clinic.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on course design; the student meets its effect

headingPath: Context and purposes of an Osteopathy degree

statements.appliesTo: osteopathy's inclusive learning community
statements.about: anticipatory design and care for self and others
statements.paraphrase: Effective anticipatory design gives a supportive cultural and institutional setting for teaching, learning and research in which people are encouraged to take on challenges, and builds the capacity to work with the discomfort of new perspectives, knowledge and skills; this requires the learning community to develop and promote ways of caring for self and others, with sustained attention to emotional, mental and physical wellbeing.

forPractitioner.text: Provide a supportive cultural and institutional context that helps people stay with the discomfort of new perspectives and skills; this requires the community to develop and promote ways of caring for self and others and to attend to emotional, mental and physical wellbeing.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be part of a community that is required to develop ways of caring for yourself and others, so that you can cope with the discomfort of meeting new ideas and learning new skills.

headingPath: Context and purposes of an Osteopathy degree

statements.appliesTo: all modes of teaching, learning and assessment
statements.about: accessibility in every mode of teaching, learning and assessment
statements.paraphrase: Blended digital and face-to-face, live and recorded teaching can make learning fair and accessible, though students' engagement varies with caring duties, disabilities, special educational needs or poor digital access; wherever possible all teaching, learning and assessment will rest on a concern for accessibility, such as captions, recordings and accessible virtual environments, with subject specialists choosing the means; supportive measures have to be put in place without weakening the regulation that keeps patients safe.

forPractitioner.text: Wherever possible, underpin every mode of teaching, learning and assessment with a concern for accessibility (captioning, recording live sessions, accessible VLE design), choose the means as subject specialists and put supportive measures in place without weakening the regulation that keeps patients safe.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on course delivery; the student meets its effect and arranges adjustments with the course

statements.appliesTo: the osteopathic learning environment
statements.about: UNESCO sustainability competencies in the learning environment
statements.paraphrase: All eight UNESCO sustainability competencies are held essential to the sustainability of osteopathy; qualified osteopaths need to use them all in practice, so the osteopathic learning environment requires them to be shown and modelled in learning facilities and curricula.

forPractitioner.text: Make all eight UNESCO sustainability competencies visible and modelled in learning facilities and curricula: the issuer says practice needs them all and the learning environment therefore requires them.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the learning environment and curriculum; the student meets its effect

headingPath: Context and purposes of an Osteopathy degree

statements.appliesTo: undergraduate osteopathic training
statements.about: personal and social responsibility as a developmental aim
statements.paraphrase: To build learning environments that advance sustainable development, undergraduate training aims to set theory and professional provision in their social, economic and political context and to promote graduates' employability; growing a sense of responsibility, personal and social, for one's own and others' well-being should be a developmental aim, and guidance from QAA and Advance HE gives more on education for sustainable development.

forPractitioner.text: Set theoretical learning and professional provision in their social, economic and political context and promote employability; treat personal and social responsibility for others' and one's own well-being as a developmental aim (should).

forBeneficiary.text: You should grow in your sense of responsibility for your own and other people's well-being, and see your future practice in its social, economic and political setting.

headingPath: Context and purposes of an Osteopathy degree

statements.appliesTo: osteopathy graduates
statements.paraphrase: Osteopathy graduates can collect, analyse and handle varied data and should understand the commercial and practical worth of their skills and be able to explain and show them to employers and when planning self-employment, private practice or more study; they should also be encouraged to become aware of their own enterprising capabilities and to apply them flexibly as contexts change.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates should understand the commercial and practical value of their skills and be able to articulate and show it to employers and in plans for their own practice or further study; courses should encourage awareness of their enterprising and entrepreneurial capabilities and the motivation to apply them flexibly.

forBeneficiary.text: You should understand what your skills are worth, commercially and practically, and be able to explain and show them to employers or when planning your own practice or further study; you should also come to recognise your own enterprising strengths and use them flexibly.

statements.about: digital competency used creatively and accessibly
statements.paraphrase: Building digital competence and transferable skills should take in the use of digital technology to share ideas creatively, innovatively and accessibly, to support academic success and employability.

forPractitioner.text: Develop digital competency and transferable skills through using digital tools to get ideas across creatively, innovatively and accessibly, for academic success and employability.

forBeneficiary.text: You should use digital tools to share your ideas creatively and accessibly, which will help both your studies and your career.

headingPath: Context and purposes of an Osteopathy degree

statements.appliesTo: curriculum design
statements.about: employability and enterprise in curriculum design
statements.paraphrase: Developing these professional knowledge, skills and competencies should be a central part of curriculum design and can be spread across the training; outcomes, teaching and authentic assessment for employability and enterprise may sit in dedicated modules and be embedded across others.

forPractitioner.text: Make professional, employability and enterprise development a key part of curriculum design across the programme, with outcomes, activities and authentic assessment in dedicated modules and embedded in others.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on curriculum design; the student meets its effect

headingPath: Context and purposes of an Osteopathy degree

statements.appliesTo: teaching on osteopathy courses
statements.about: external speakers and alumni in teaching
statements.paraphrase: Bringing in external speakers, members of the profession and alumni to enrich teaching and share first-hand experience is recommended; meeting a range of osteopaths builds awareness of the working context and can strengthen graduates' ability to handle market forces and promote themselves ethically.

forPractitioner.text: Involve external speakers, practitioners and alumni in teaching (the issuer recommends it), so students meet varied osteopaths and grow ready to handle the market and present themselves ethically.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a recommendation to the course on its teaching

statements.appliesTo: osteopathy courses and their students
statements.about: clinical reasoning, supervised experience and autonomy in learning
statements.paraphrase: Academic and theoretical learning progresses through levels in line with the Quality Code and spans procedural, propositional and psychomotor knowledge within a clinical framework; practical and clinical reasoning skills should firmly support clinical decisions and safe, effective practice that keeps students fit to practise; supervised clinical experience is essential and autonomy in learning is required for lifelong learning and reflection; enough knowledge of UK healthcare, business and regulation lets graduates work independently.

forPractitioner.text: Design progression aligned to the Quality Code across procedural, propositional and psychomotor knowledge; make applied and clinical reasoning robustly support safe, effective decisions and continuing fitness to practise; provide supervised clinical experience and require autonomy in learning.

forBeneficiary.text: Your practical and clinical reasoning skills should firmly support safe, effective decisions about patients and keep you fit to practise; supervised clinic work is central, and you will need to take charge of your own learning.

statements.appliesTo: osteopathy courses and their graduates
statements.about: core sciences, communication and patient-centred teaching
statements.paraphrase: As a primary healthcare profession, osteopathy needs students to graduate with full knowledge and understanding of anatomy, physiology and pathology and excellent communication and interpersonal skills for working with patients and other professionals; teaching and learning should stress patient-centred care, including a full grasp of psychosocial factors, to support the patient's journey.

forPractitioner.text: Ensure graduates leave with comprehensive anatomy, physiology and pathology and excellent communication and interpersonal skills; teaching and learning should emphasise patient-centred care, psychosocial factors included.

forBeneficiary.text: You will need a thorough knowledge of anatomy, physiology and pathology and excellent communication skills, and your teaching should put the patient, with their psychological and social circumstances, at the centre.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: graduates of pre-registration osteopathy courses
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to show they are a competent practitioner with strong practical skills (manual therapy among them) and the problem-solving to draw on varied approaches for different presentations.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will be competent, with highly developed practical and manual therapy skills and problem-solving across approaches for different presentations.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be a competent practitioner with strong hands-on and manual therapy skills, able to solve problems using a range of approaches for different patients.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: graduates of pre-registration osteopathy courses
statements.about: integrating many factors in whole-person care
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to show a developed knowledge base and clinical ability that lets them bring many factors together in a full, overall approach to a person's health needs.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will have a developed knowledge base and the clinical ability to integrate multiple factors into a comprehensive approach to each person's health needs.

forBeneficiary.text: You will have the knowledge and clinical ability to bring many factors together and look at a patient's health needs as a whole.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: graduates of pre-registration osteopathy courses
statements.about: a caring partnership with the patient
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to show they are caring, empathetic and trustworthy and can work as the patient's partner.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will be caring, empathetic and trustworthy and able to work in partnership with patients.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be caring, empathetic and trustworthy, and work with patients as partners.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: graduates of pre-registration osteopathy courses
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to show professional attitudes, values and behaviour fitting a healthcare practitioner, including on consent, safeguarding and candour.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will hold the attitudes, values and behaviours of a healthcare practitioner, including consent, safeguarding and candour.

forBeneficiary.text: You will act with the attitudes, values and behaviour expected of a health professional, including on consent, safeguarding and honesty when things go wrong.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: graduates of pre-registration osteopathy courses
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to show they are reflective, self-aware and enquiring, and committed to learning throughout life.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will be reflective, self-aware and enquiring and committed to lifelong learning.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be reflective, self-aware and curious, and committed to learning throughout your career.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: graduates of pre-registration osteopathy courses
statements.about: the scope and limits of osteopathy and of oneself
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to show they value osteopathy's role in treating patients of every age while knowing the limits of its scope, above all in relation to their own knowledge and abilities.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will appreciate osteopathy's role across all ages and know the limits of its scope, especially those set by their own knowledge and capability.

forBeneficiary.text: You will value what osteopathy can do for patients of all ages and know where its limits lie, especially the limits of your own knowledge and skill.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: competent students on graduation
statements.paraphrase: Competent students will build core knowledge, understanding and skill and be able to apply them to evaluating and managing patients, graduating as safe, rounded practitioners; the outcomes in 3.6 set out the detail and are designed to show the capabilities needed to register as an osteopath in the UK under the OPS and the regulator's graduate outcomes.

forPractitioner.text: Competent students will build core knowledge, understanding and skill and be able to use them in evaluating and managing patients, graduating as safe, rounded practitioners; 3.6 sets out the detail against the registration requirements.

forBeneficiary.text: You will build the core knowledge, understanding and skills of osteopathy and be able to use them to assess and care for patients, so that you graduate as a safe, all-round practitioner ready to register.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will have a detailed, joined-up knowledge of how the human body is built and works, centred on the neuromusculoskeletal system, enough to tell normal variation from abnormal structure and process in living people.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will know human anatomy and physiology in integrated detail, above all the neuromusculoskeletal system, well enough to tell normal variation from pathology in a living patient.

forBeneficiary.text: You will know in detail how the body is built and how it works, especially muscles, bones, joints and nerves, so that you can tell normal variation from something abnormal in a living person.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.about: disease knowledge for judgement and referral
statements.paraphrase: Will know enough current science and medicine about human disease to guide clinical judgement on examination and palpation findings and to spot conditions that need referral for further tests or other professional help.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will hold current scientific and medical knowledge of disease, enough to support judgement about examination and palpatory findings and to identify when a patient needs referring on.

forBeneficiary.text: You will know enough about disease to make sense of what you find when you examine and palpate a patient, and to notice when someone needs referring for tests or other professional help.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will know the psychology and sociology that bear on gaining and keeping health, and appreciate each person's needs, values and beliefs, enough to frame clinical decisions and patient management.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will know the psychology and sociology relevant to health and appreciate individual needs, values and beliefs, as context for their clinical decisions and management of patients.

forBeneficiary.text: You will understand the psychological and social side of health and respect each patient's needs, values and beliefs, so that they shape the decisions you make about care.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will know the neurophysiology of pain and the psychosocial influences on it, and how both affect the patient and the way their problem presents.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will know pain neurophysiology and the psychosocial factors in pain, and how these shape the patient's experience and clinical picture.

forBeneficiary.text: You will understand how pain works in the nervous system, how psychological and social factors affect it, and how both change what a patient experiences and shows you.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.about: the role of touch in treatment
statements.paraphrase: Will understand what touch does within treatment and how it can affect the way patients respond to osteopathic techniques.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will understand the place of touch in treatment and how it can shape patients' responses to techniques.

forBeneficiary.text: You will understand the part touch plays in treatment and how it can change the way a patient responds to what you do.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.about: concerns hidden behind the presenting problem
statements.paraphrase: Will recognise that the problem a patient brings may hide other health concerns, physical and behavioural.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will recognise that a presenting complaint can conceal underlying physical or behavioural health issues.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be alert to the chance that the problem a patient comes with may be hiding another health issue, physical or behavioural.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will know how to choose, use well and monitor a suitable range of osteopathic techniques and management approaches for each patient, taking account of relative and absolute contraindications.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will know how to select, apply and monitor osteopathic techniques and management suited to the individual, alert to relative and absolute contraindications.

forBeneficiary.text: You will know how to pick, carry out and keep track of the right osteopathic techniques and ways of managing care for each patient, and when a technique should not be used.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will know and understand research methodology and be able to appraise critically how good numerical and qualitative clinical studies are, enough to guide clinical decisions and patient management.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will understand research methodologies and critically judge the quality of clinical studies of either kind, numerical or qualitative, so that evidence informs their decisions and care.

forBeneficiary.text: You will understand how clinical research is done and be able to judge how good a study is, whether numerical or qualitative, so that evidence guides your decisions about patients.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will understand critically the principles and concepts of osteopathy and how they can guide rational clinical decisions.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will have a critical grasp of osteopathic principles and concepts and how they can support reasoned clinical decision-making.

forBeneficiary.text: You will understand the principles and ideas of osteopathy critically and know how they can guide sound clinical decisions.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.about: models of health, disease and illness
statements.paraphrase: Will understand models of health, disease and illness and how they shape critical thinking about practical care and management of patients.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will understand models of health, disease and illness and use them to think critically about patient care and management.

forBeneficiary.text: You will understand different ways of thinking about health, disease and illness and use them to think critically about how you care for patients.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will be critically aware of the principles, perspectives and practice of other relevant health professions and able to adapt them.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will be critically aware of how other relevant health professions think and work, and will adapt what is useful from them.

forBeneficiary.text: You will know, critically, how other health professions think and work, and be able to adapt what is useful from them in your own practice.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will understand how osteopathic principles are put into practice through different treatment and management approaches, and how to choose or adapt techniques to suit an individual patient's needs and preferences.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will understand how principles translate into varied osteopathic treatment and management, and how to choose or adapt techniques for the individual's needs and preferences.

forBeneficiary.text: You will understand how osteopathic principles show up in different treatments, and how to choose or adjust techniques to suit each patient's needs and wishes.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will understand the different models of the therapeutic relationship.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will understand a range of models of the therapeutic relationship.

forBeneficiary.text: You will understand the different ways of thinking about the relationship between practitioner and patient.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.about: elements and boundaries of the therapeutic relationship
statements.paraphrase: Will show the parts and limits of a therapeutic relationship, with the skills to build a fitting partnership with the patient.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will demonstrate what a therapeutic relationship involves and where its boundaries lie, with the skills to build a proper partnership with each patient.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to show what a good therapeutic relationship involves and where its limits lie, and build a proper partnership with each patient.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will show the self-awareness to spot possible boundary problems and handle them well, so that care stays at a proper standard.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will show the self-awareness to identify and manage potential boundary issues effectively, keeping standards of care intact.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be self-aware enough to notice when a boundary issue might be arising and deal with it well, so your patient's care does not suffer.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will cope well and promptly with the unfamiliar or uncertain, being open with patients when things go wrong and aware enough of themselves to manage the case honestly.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will deal effectively with unfamiliar situations and uncertainty, apply the duty of candour and manage the case with integrity and self-awareness.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to handle situations that are new or uncertain, be open and honest with patients when something goes wrong, and manage the case with integrity.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to defend sound strategies for handling the ethical problems a practitioner is likely to meet.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will justify acceptable strategies for managing the ethical issues practitioners commonly face.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to explain and defend how you would handle the ethical problems you are likely to meet in practice.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will keep patient information confidential and act only with informed consent from the patient or someone able to consent for them, unless safeguarding concerns take precedence.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will maintain confidentiality and act only on informed consent from the patient or an authorised person, save where safeguarding overrides it.

forBeneficiary.text: You will keep patients' information confidential and act only with their informed consent, or that of someone who can consent for them, except where a safeguarding concern comes first.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will use suitable ways of looking after their own physical and psychological well-being while working with patients, to stay professionally effective.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will use suitable physical and psychological self-care strategies in patient work to sustain professional effectiveness.

forBeneficiary.text: You will look after your own physical and mental well-being while treating patients, so that you can keep working at your best.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.about: forms of communication and adapting them
statements.paraphrase: Will understand the kinds of human communication and what each does well and badly, and be able to switch between them with patients and colleagues to suit the person.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will understand the forms of communication and their strengths and limits, and shift between them with patients and colleagues to fit the individual.

forBeneficiary.text: You will understand different ways people communicate, what each does well and less well, and switch between them to suit the patient or colleague in front of you.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will be skilled at linking, combining and acting on information gathered by verbal and non-verbal means, in person or through telehealth and online meetings.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will relate, integrate and respond to information gathered verbally and non-verbally, face to face or by telehealth and online.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be good at picking up, combining and responding to what patients tell you and show you, in person or online.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will be building a full vocabulary that turns what is felt in palpation into suitable language for clear communication with colleagues, other professionals and patients.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will be developing a full vocabulary to put palpatory findings into words suited to colleagues, other professionals and patients.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be building the vocabulary to put what you feel with your hands into clear words for patients, colleagues and other professionals.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.about: speaking critically about osteopathy and its claims
statements.paraphrase: Will talk about osteopathy from a critical, reasoned standpoint, covering its limits, strengths and potential, weighing research, opinion and anecdote to judge therapeutic claims and better inform patients.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will discuss osteopathy critically, including its limits, strengths and potential, weighing research against opinion and anecdote to assess therapeutic claims for patients.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to talk about osteopathy critically, including what it cannot do as well as what it can, and weigh research against opinion and anecdote when telling patients what to expect.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.about: digital literacy for running a practice
statements.paraphrase: Will be digitally literate enough to run a modern osteopathic practice efficiently: working with other health professionals, writing good reports and presentations for referral, using technology for research and clinic tasks, handling financial and other data for legal compliance and analysing data of both kinds for audit.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will have the digital literacy to run a modern practice: liaising with other professionals, producing high-quality referral reports and presentations, using technology for research and clinical work, managing financial and compliance data and analysing data for audit.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be confident with the digital side of running a practice: working with other health professionals, writing good referral reports, using technology for research and clinic work, keeping financial and legal records and analysing data for audit.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.about: case history and analysis of the complaint
statements.paraphrase: Will show effective, efficient taking of a detailed case history and analysis of the presenting complaint.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will demonstrate effective, efficient detailed case-history taking and analysis of the presenting complaint.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to take a detailed case history efficiently and analyse the problem the patient has come with.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will recognise how much the psychosocial setting of the complaint matters and the part shared decision-making plays in planning treatment.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will recognise the weight of a complaint's psychosocial context and the part shared decisions play in planning treatment.

forBeneficiary.text: You will recognise how much a patient's life and circumstances matter to their problem, and how deciding together shapes the treatment plan.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will identify the patient's needs and arrange specific clinical investigations or other referrals where needed.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will identify patients' needs and arrange specific investigations or referrals as needed.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to work out what a patient needs and arrange tests or referrals when they are called for.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will carry out a thorough, continuing evaluation of the patient, possibly including biomechanical, psychosocial, attitudinal, palpatory and clinical examination, as suits and respects the person's presentation.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will evaluate patients thoroughly and continuously, using biomechanical, psychosocial, attitudinal, palpatory and clinical examination as the presentation warrants.

forBeneficiary.text: You will examine each patient thoroughly and keep reassessing them, using physical, psychological, hands-on and clinical tests as fits their situation.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will produce several hypotheses for the presenting complaint to support a treatment plan or onward referral, with an explanation of the working diagnosis the patient can follow.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will generate several hypotheses for the complaint to inform a plan or referral, and explain the working diagnosis accessibly.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to come up with several possible explanations for a patient's problem, use them to plan treatment or refer on, and explain your working diagnosis in words they understand.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.about: non-verbal cues, protected characteristics and socioeconomic status
statements.paraphrase: Will recognise the features and effects of non-verbal communication, and how protected characteristics and socioeconomic status may bear on the patient's health.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will recognise what non-verbal communication shows and how protected characteristics and socioeconomic status can affect health.

forBeneficiary.text: You will notice what patients communicate without words and understand how things like their background, identity and income can affect their health.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will produce full, accurate records of what the patient evaluation found.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will generate complete, accurate records of evaluation outcomes.

forBeneficiary.text: You will keep full and accurate records of what you find when you assess a patient.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.about: the therapeutic value of touch and palpation
statements.paraphrase: Will appraise critically what touch and palpation contribute to diagnosis and treatment.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will critically appraise the therapeutic value of touch and palpation in diagnosis and treatment.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to judge critically what touch and palpation add to diagnosing and treating patients.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.about: talking with patients about touch and consent
statements.paraphrase: Will be aware that one must keep talking with the patient about touch and palpation, to confirm findings and to secure consent and comfort.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will be aware of the need for continuing dialogue with patients about touch and palpation, to confirm findings and keep consent and comfort.

forBeneficiary.text: You will keep talking with patients about how and why you are touching them, to check your findings and make sure they consent and are comfortable.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will use criticality to recognise and understand tissue structure and function when palpating during evaluation.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will apply criticality in palpation to recognise and understand tissue structure and function during evaluation.

forBeneficiary.text: You will think critically about what you feel when you palpate, recognising how the tissues are built and working.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.about: palpation as diagnostic and therapeutic technique
statements.paraphrase: Will use palpation both to help diagnosis and as a therapeutic technique that reassures patients.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will use palpation as a complementary diagnostic tool and as a reassuring therapeutic technique.

forBeneficiary.text: You will use palpation both to help work out what is wrong and as a way of treating and reassuring patients.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will show sensitivity in palpation, knowing its limits and seeing continuing chances to develop the skill.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will palpate with sensitivity, aware of its limits and of continuing ways to develop the skill.

forBeneficiary.text: You will palpate with sensitivity, know the limits of what it tells you and keep looking for ways to improve.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will record palpatory findings accurately, consistently and suitably alongside objective measures and outcomes reported by patients.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will record palpatory findings accurately and consistently, alongside objective measures and patient-reported outcomes.

forBeneficiary.text: You will record what you find by palpation accurately and consistently, next to objective measures and what the patient reports.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will combine palpation with other evaluation methods to shape a working diagnostic hypothesis and a continuing treatment plan.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will use palpation with other assessment methods to inform a working diagnosis and ongoing plan.

forBeneficiary.text: You will combine palpation with other ways of assessing a patient to form a working diagnosis and plan.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will analyse and reflect in detail on what history taking and evaluation have produced.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will analyse and reflect in detail on information from history taking and evaluation.

forBeneficiary.text: You will analyse and reflect carefully on what you learned from the case history and examination.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.about: hypotheses on the cause of the complaint
statements.paraphrase: Will generate and justify a set of hypotheses about the cause of the presenting complaint.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will generate and justify hypotheses for the aetiology of the presenting complaint.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to put forward and justify possible causes for the patient's problem.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.about: telling patients or guardians about findings
statements.paraphrase: Will work out how to tell the patient, or a person with parental responsibility or guardianship, about findings and talk through possible courses of action.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will establish how to share findings with the patient or a parent or guardian and discuss the options.

forBeneficiary.text: You will know how to explain your findings to a patient, or to a parent or guardian, and talk through the options.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will weigh suitable courses of action through rational, shared decision-making that critically considers the limits of their own competence and the likely effects of treatment.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will consider options through rational, shared decision-making, critically weighing their own limits of competence and treatment's likely effects.

forBeneficiary.text: You will weigh up options with the patient in a reasoned way, thinking critically about the limits of your own competence and what treatment is likely to do.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will, with consent from the patient or someone who can consent for them, refer to other health professionals for further investigation where needed.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will refer patients to other health professionals for further investigation when needed, with proper consent.

forBeneficiary.text: You will refer patients to other health professionals for further tests when needed, with their consent or that of someone who can consent for them.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will draw up a treatment plan and prognosis that tracks the effect of treatment during and after each session across the planned course of care.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will formulate a plan and prognosis that monitors treatment effects during and after application over the planned course.

forBeneficiary.text: You will draw up a treatment plan and prognosis and keep checking how treatment is working, during and after each session.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will identify and reflect on what is holding back progress and plan and act on it.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will identify and reflect on obstacles to progress and plan and take suitable action.

forBeneficiary.text: You will spot and think about what is getting in the way of a patient's progress, then plan and act on it.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will show awareness of, and the ability to choose from, the wide range of direct and indirect osteopathic techniques to suit the patient, guided by the best evidence available.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will demonstrate knowledge of, and choice among, the full range of direct and indirect techniques, matched to the patient and guided by best evidence.

forBeneficiary.text: You will know the wide range of direct and indirect osteopathic techniques and be able to choose the right ones for each patient, guided by the best evidence.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.about: patient management agreed with the patient
statements.paraphrase: Will show awareness and use of a range of management approaches agreed with the patient, taking account of their preferences and needs.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will demonstrate a range of patient management approaches developed with the patient and responsive to their preferences and needs.

forBeneficiary.text: You will use a range of ways of managing a patient's care, worked out with them and shaped by what they need and prefer.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will reason through the indications and contraindications for specific techniques or their modification.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will rationalise indications and contraindications for specific techniques and their adaptations.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to explain when a particular technique, or a changed version of it, is or is not suitable.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will adapt osteopathic approaches and justify or change how they are used in response to the patient's feedback, as person-centred care.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will adapt approaches and justify or amend their use in response to patient feedback, as person-centred intervention.

forBeneficiary.text: You will adjust your approach in response to how the patient reacts, and be able to explain why.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will watch for spontaneous changes so as to spot and record adverse reactions to treatment, and respond suitably, referring on where needed.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will monitor for and record adverse reactions to treatment and respond suitably, including by referral.

forBeneficiary.text: You will watch for and record any unwanted reactions to treatment and respond properly, including referring the patient on if needed.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will keep an open, enquiring mind about the results of treatment.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will maintain an open-minded, enquiring stance towards treatment outcomes.

forBeneficiary.text: You will stay open-minded and curious about how your treatments turn out.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will write down evaluation findings and what they mean accurately, legibly and accessibly in each patient's notes.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will write evaluation findings and what they mean into case notes accurately, legibly and accessibly.

forBeneficiary.text: You will write up what you found and what you think it means clearly and accurately in each patient's notes.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.about: outcome data for an individual patient
statements.paraphrase: Will collect and organise a full range of data, outcome measures and evidence of both kinds on how an individual patient responds to treatment.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will gather and organise qualitative and quantitative data, outcome measures and evidence on a patient's response to treatment.

forBeneficiary.text: You will collect and organise numbers, measures and patients' own accounts to show how someone is responding to treatment.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will work with a critical grasp of the main ideas behind health education and promotion and how they are organised in the UK and abroad.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will work with a critical appreciation of the concepts and organisation of health education and promotion at home and abroad.

forBeneficiary.text: You will understand critically how health education and health promotion work, in the UK and elsewhere.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.about: social and cultural factors in health choices
statements.paraphrase: Will understand how far psychosocial, cultural and socioeconomic factors matter in helping patients make informed choices about looking after their health.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will understand the bearing of psychosocial, cultural and socioeconomic factors on patients' informed choices about their own health maintenance.

forBeneficiary.text: You will understand how people's circumstances, culture and income affect the choices they make about their health, and use this to help them choose well.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will work with the patient to agree self-care, which may cover diet, exercise and changes to lifestyle.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will work in partnership with patients to identify self-care, such as dietary advice, exercise and lifestyle change.

forBeneficiary.text: You will work with patients to agree what they can do for themselves, such as diet, exercise and changes to daily life.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will give realistic advice on where to find local health-promoting activities and how to use them well, in keeping with community, cultural and ethnic values.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will offer realistic advice on local health-promoting activities that respects community, cultural and ethnic values.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to point patients to realistic local activities that support their health, in ways that respect their community and culture.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will look after their own health and well-being and carefully follow the procedures for managing communicable disease.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will care for their own health and follow due diligence and procedures for communicable disease.

forBeneficiary.text: You will look after your own health and follow infection-control procedures carefully.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will identify what referring a patient to other practitioners or services could gain and where it falls short.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will identify the potential benefits and limits of referring patients to other practitioners or services.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to weigh up what a patient could gain from being referred elsewhere, and what the drawbacks might be.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will be committed to learning throughout life, building skills and knowledge through reflection and active approaches.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will commit to lifelong learning, gaining skills and knowledge through reflective and active approaches.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be committed to learning throughout your career, using reflection and active practice to keep building your skills and knowledge.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.about: awareness of what safe care demands
statements.paraphrase: Will be critically aware of the practical skill and clinical knowledge needed to give the expected standard of care.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will be critically aware of the level of practical skill and clinical knowledge the expected standards of care require.

forBeneficiary.text: You will know, critically, what level of practical skill and clinical knowledge good care demands of you.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to weigh up their own strengths and weaknesses, personal and professional, so as to plan and carry out continuing self-directed development and learning.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will reflect on their strengths and limits and plan and carry out ongoing self-directed development.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to reflect on your strengths and weaknesses, plan how to develop and follow your plan through.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to record reflection on clinical practice in a professional portfolio, enough to show continuing professional development to the statutory regulator.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will record reflective activity on clinical practice in a portfolio that evidences CPD for the statutory regulator.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to record your reflections on clinical practice in a portfolio that shows your professional development to the regulator.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to contribute to or understand research and other scholarship in support of personal and professional growth.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will contribute to, or understand, research and scholarly activity that supports their personal and professional development.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to take part in, or make sense of, research and other scholarly work to help you grow personally and professionally.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will show critical problem-solving skill at a level that guides the reading of clinical and other data and supports sound clinical reasoning and decisions.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will evidence critical problem-solving that informs interpretation of clinical and other data and supports clinical reasoning and decisions.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to solve problems critically, so that you read clinical information well and reason soundly about what to do.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will show engagement in peer review, giving respectful feedback and discussion that lets colleagues work together for their own and the profession's development.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will evidence peer review and respectful feedback that supports collaborative group work for individual and professional development.

forBeneficiary.text: You will take part in peer review, giving and receiving feedback respectfully so that you and your colleagues improve together.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.about: self-care and self-awareness for safe care
statements.paraphrase: Will have the self-care and self-awareness to keep giving patients an acceptable standard of care consistently.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will show self-care and self-awareness enough to sustain an acceptable standard of patient care.

forBeneficiary.text: You will look after yourself and know yourself well enough to keep your care of patients at a good standard.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will have the attitudes and skills needed to meet continuing fitness to practise requirements in full and keep their registration.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will have the attitudes and skills to comply fully with continuing fitness to practise requirements and stay registered.

forBeneficiary.text: You will have the attitudes and skills to keep meeting fitness to practise requirements, so you can stay on the register.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will understand what statutory regulation, as authorised by Parliament, is and why it matters.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will understand the concept and importance of statutory regulation of the profession.

forBeneficiary.text: You will understand what it means for your profession to be regulated by law, and why that matters.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will keep to the professional standards in the OPS and the other guidance from the General Osteopathic Council and other relevant bodies.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will abide by the OPS and other guidance from the GOsC and other appropriate bodies.

forBeneficiary.text: You will follow the regulator's professional standards and other guidance for osteopaths.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will practise safely, competently and effectively within the law, for example complying with legislation on consent, safeguarding, equality, diversity and inclusion, data protection and health and safety.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will practise safely, competently and effectively within the law, including consent, safeguarding, equality, data protection and health and safety legislation.

forBeneficiary.text: You will practise safely, competently and effectively within the law, including the rules on consent, safeguarding, equality, data protection and health and safety.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will act promptly to prevent harm, whether by managing the situation alone, consulting a colleague or reporting to a suitable authority; acting where patient safety may be at risk covers candour with patients, safeguarding law, colleagues putting patients at risk, practitioner health and reporting conduct or competence to the regulator.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will act quickly to prevent harm, alone, with a colleague or by reporting, covering candour, safeguarding, reports to the regulator and concerns about colleagues or their own health.

forBeneficiary.text: You will act quickly to prevent harm: dealing with it yourself, talking to a colleague or reporting it, including being open with patients, safeguarding, raising concerns about colleagues or your own health and reporting to the regulator.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will respect and protect patients' dignity, autonomy and confidentiality.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will respect and uphold patient dignity, autonomy and confidentiality.

forBeneficiary.text: You will respect and protect each patient's dignity, independence and privacy.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will be open about their actions to others and justify them when appropriate.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will disclose and justify their actions to others when appropriate.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be open about what you have done and be able to explain why, when that is called for.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will take responsibility for keeping professional boundaries and maintain high personal and professional conduct and the profession's integrity.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will take responsibility for professional boundaries and uphold high standards of conduct and the profession's integrity.

forBeneficiary.text: You will take responsibility for keeping professional boundaries and for behaving well, personally and professionally, so the profession can be trusted.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.about: healthcare delivery and osteopathy's place in it
statements.paraphrase: Will critically understand how healthcare is delivered in the UK and abroad and what osteopathy contributes, as an Allied Health Profession in NHS England and as primary healthcare.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will critically understand UK and overseas healthcare delivery and osteopathy's contribution, as an Allied Health Profession in NHS England and as primary care.

forBeneficiary.text: You will understand critically how healthcare is organised in the UK and elsewhere, and where osteopathy fits, including as an allied health profession and in primary care.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will critically understand what a range of conventional and non-conventional health professions claim and how this relates to osteopathic practice.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will critically understand the claims of conventional and non-conventional health professions and their relation to osteopathy.

forBeneficiary.text: You will understand critically what other health professions, mainstream and not, claim to do and how that relates to osteopathy.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will show critical evaluation of what osteopathic practice currently claims, in the UK and abroad.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will demonstrate critical evaluation of current claims made for osteopathic practice at home and abroad.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to judge critically what osteopathy currently claims to achieve, in the UK and elsewhere.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.about: financial and practice management within the law
statements.paraphrase: Will understand the financial and operational detail of managing a practice within legal and ethical requirements, including health and safety, employment law and other relevant guidance or law.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will understand financial and operational practice management within legal and ethical requirements, including health and safety and employment law.

forBeneficiary.text: You will understand the money and day-to-day running of a practice within the law and ethics, including health and safety and employment rules.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will understand audit's part in checking the quality of practice and be able to help produce operational and strategic plans.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will understand audit's role in monitoring practice quality and contribute to operational and strategic planning.

forBeneficiary.text: You will understand how audit checks the quality of a practice and be able to help plan how a practice runs and develops.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
