statements.paraphrase: Will keep patient records and information in line with what law and ethics require on confidentiality and peer support.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will maintain records and information that meet the legal and ethical duties of confidentiality and of peer support.

forBeneficiary.text: You will keep patient records and information in a way that meets legal and ethical rules on confidentiality.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.paraphrase: Will keep effective, high-standard contact with outside agencies, including referrals to health professionals in and beyond the NHS, insurers and public services.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will generate effective, high-standard contact with external agencies, including referrals within and outside the NHS, insurers and public services.

forBeneficiary.text: You will deal effectively and professionally with outside organisations, such as the NHS, other health professionals, insurers and public services.

headingPath: The key characteristics of graduates in Osteopathy

statements.appliesTo: students on successful completion of a pre-registration osteopathy course
statements.about: business skills for a viable practice
statements.paraphrase: Will show knowledge of the business skills needed to set up a viable osteopathic business that puts patients before profit.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will demonstrate the business knowledge needed to establish a viable practice that puts patients ahead of profit.

forBeneficiary.text: You will know the business skills needed to set up a practice that works financially while putting patients before profit.

statements.appliesTo: students of osteopathy
statements.about: reflective, leadership, peer review and lifelong learning skills
statements.paraphrase: Knowledge, skills and experience build up across the course; teaching and learning will take a critical, reflective approach to osteopathy with attention to its concepts, principles and personalised care; students will gain reflective, leadership, peer review and lifelong learning skills; joining theory and practice prepares them to work autonomously, and methods suit diverse learning styles and are delivered sustainably and inclusively.

forPractitioner.text: Teaching and learning will be critical and reflective about osteopathic concepts, principles and personalised care; students will gain reflective, leadership, peer-review and lifelong learning skills, and methods suit diverse learners and are delivered sustainably and inclusively.

forBeneficiary.text: You will learn in a critical, reflective way and gain skills in reflection, leadership, peer review and lifelong learning that prepare you to practise on your own.

statements.appliesTo: assessment on pre-registration courses
statements.about: assessment towards the OPS; the condition to graduate
statements.paraphrase: Assessment strategies should support students' development as practitioners and in the end let them show they meet the OPS; only students who meet those standards may graduate.

forPractitioner.text: Design assessment that supports development and finally enables students to demonstrate they meet the OPS; only those who meet them graduate.

forBeneficiary.text: Your assessments should help you develop as a practitioner and let you show that you meet the professional standards; you will only graduate once you have met them.

statements.appliesTo: assessment strategies
statements.about: authentic assessment shaped by practitioners and patients
statements.paraphrase: Assessment strategies should match the range and depth of competence the OPS requires and relate, where possible, to real situations and practice; experienced, qualified educators and practitioners should lead their design, with the patient voice in support.

forPractitioner.text: Make assessment reflect the range and depth of OPS competence and real practice where possible; involve experienced educators and practitioners centrally, supported by the patient voice.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course in designing assessment

statements.appliesTo: assessment tools
statements.paraphrase: A varied range of assessment tools should be used to support learning and development and different learning styles and differences; they should be valid and reliable and give a clear, supportive path to progression, with formative and summative assessment and the involvement of peers, patients, educators and outside experts where suitable at the centre.

forPractitioner.text: Use varied, valid and reliable assessment tools that support different learners and give a transparent path to progression, centred on formative and summative assessment and involving peers, patients, educators and external expertise where suitable.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course in choosing assessment

statements.appliesTo: assessment and the students it serves
statements.about: assessment that tracks growing complexity towards autonomy
statements.paraphrase: Assessment should mirror the rising complexity and responsibility of study and the demands of the OPS, supporting students from novice to competent practitioner, when they will need to manage clinical uncertainty and show the qualities and competence of an autonomous practitioner able to work in many settings.

forPractitioner.text: Assessment should track rising complexity and responsibility and the OPS requirements, supporting the move from novice to competent practitioner able to handle clinical uncertainty and act autonomously across settings.

forBeneficiary.text: Your assessments should grow more demanding as you progress, helping you move from beginner to competent practitioner who can handle clinical uncertainty and work independently in different settings.

statements.appliesTo: each higher education provider
statements.about: achievement above threshold and Annex D
statements.paraphrase: Most students will do well above the minimum threshold standards; each provider has its own way of deciding what counts as evidence of this and should refer to Annex D of the UK qualifications frameworks.

forPractitioner.text: Expect most students to exceed the threshold; set your own method for judging evidence of higher achievement and refer to Annex D of the Frameworks for Higher Education Qualifications.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider in judging achievement above the threshold; the student-facing point is the threshold list at 6.10

statements.appliesTo: students and osteopaths
statements.paraphrase: Students develop the skills to engage critically with evidence-informed practice in its three parts, namely research, clinical experience and what patients expect; they are expected to judge how clinically relevant published research is and to carry out audits, service evaluations and research to improve practice, care and current professional issues; in any setting osteopaths are expected to back and build an evidence-informed approach.

forPractitioner.text: Students develop critical engagement with research, clinical experience and patient expectations; they are expected to judge the clinical relevance of published research and to conduct audit, service evaluation and research that improve practice and care.

forBeneficiary.text: You will build the skills to weigh research, clinical experience and what patients expect, and you are expected to judge how relevant published research is and to take part in audit and research that improves care.

statements.appliesTo: osteopathy courses, graduating students and registered osteopaths
statements.about: Recognised Qualification approval and the OPS
statements.paraphrase: Osteopathy courses are approved by the regulator, the General Osteopathic Council, through Recognised Qualification status that is reviewed regularly; this requires following its graduate outcomes and education standards of September 2022 and showing that the OPS are delivered well; those graduating and those registered must meet the OPS for the whole of their careers.

forPractitioner.text: Courses gain and keep Recognised Qualification status from the GOsC through regular review, which requires following its graduate outcomes and education standards (September 2022) and delivering the OPS effectively; graduates and registrants must meet the OPS throughout their careers.

forBeneficiary.text: Throughout your career, from graduation onwards, you must meet the regulator's professional practice standards; your course is approved and regularly reviewed to make sure it prepares you for this.

statements.appliesTo: students awarded an honours degree in osteopathy
statements.paraphrase: Will have developed strong interpersonal and communication skills for dealing professionally, ethically and effectively, from an informed position, with diverse patients, peers and other health professionals; this is the minimum for the honours award.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will have developed highly effective interpersonal and communication skills for professional, ethical dealings with diverse patients, peers and other health professionals.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold for the award, you will have developed strong people and communication skills, so that you deal professionally, ethically and effectively with a wide range of patients, fellow students and other health professionals.

statements.appliesTo: students awarded an honours degree in osteopathy
statements.about: osteopathic philosophy and principles in decisions
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown a critical grasp of the philosophy, principles and concepts of osteopathy and how they can guide reasoned clinical decisions.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will have shown critical understanding of osteopathy's philosophy and principles and how these can guide rational clinical decisions.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold, you will understand the philosophy and principles of osteopathy critically and how they can guide sound clinical decisions.

statements.appliesTo: students awarded an honours degree in osteopathy
statements.about: the sciences underpinning practice across the lifespan
statements.paraphrase: Will have gained coherent, detailed knowledge and understanding of how the biological, physical and behavioural sciences behind osteopathy interrelate and apply clinically across a patient's life.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will have coherent, detailed knowledge of the interplay of biological, physical and behavioural sciences that underpin practice, and of their clinical use across the lifespan.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold, you will have a clear, detailed understanding of how the biological, physical and behavioural sciences behind osteopathy link together and apply to patients at every stage of life.

statements.appliesTo: students awarded an honours degree in osteopathy
statements.about: safe assessment, working diagnosis and shared planning
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown the ability to carry out a clinical and osteopathic assessment that lets them assess a patient safely and effectively, reach a working diagnosis and, with the patient through shared decisions, form a treatment plan that allows for physical, biopsychosocial, cultural, equality and diversity needs and the person's values, preferences and expectations.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will be able to assess a patient safely and effectively, reach a working diagnosis and agree a treatment plan through shared decision-making that respects the person's physical, psychosocial, cultural and diversity needs and their values and preferences.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold, you will be able to assess a patient safely and effectively, reach a working diagnosis and agree a treatment plan with them that takes account of their whole situation, values and wishes.

statements.appliesTo: students awarded an honours degree in osteopathy
statements.about: critical clinical reasoning with incomplete knowledge
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown a critical approach to clinical and osteopathic assessment, using problem-solving and clinical reasoning that draws on what they know, including where it may be incomplete, complex or unpredictable, to shape treatment and management plans.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will assess critically, using problem-solving and clinical reasoning drawn from their knowledge, including incomplete, complex or unpredictable areas, to plan treatment and management.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold, you will approach assessment critically, using problem-solving and clinical reasoning, even where what you know is incomplete or the picture is complex, to plan treatment.

statements.appliesTo: students awarded an honours degree in osteopathy
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown the ability to choose critically, apply and justify osteopathic treatment suited to a patient's needs, to monitor and judge its effect over the treatment plan and to guide and educate the patient as needed to help progress.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will critically select, apply and justify treatment for the individual, monitor and evaluate its effect across the plan and guide and educate the patient to support progress.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold, you will be able to choose, carry out and justify treatment that suits each patient, check and judge how well it is working and guide and teach the patient to help them progress.

statements.appliesTo: students awarded an honours degree in osteopathy
statements.about: supporting well-being across the lifespan, including long-term illness
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown they appreciate how osteopaths can support patients' well-being across the lifespan and as public health priorities change, including care that eases or supports well-being when a patient lives with lifelong illness or disability.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will appreciate osteopathy's value for well-being over the lifespan and in changing public health contexts, including palliative and supportive care for lifelong illness or disability.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold, you will appreciate how osteopathy can support people's well-being throughout life and as public health needs change, including helping people who live with long-term illness or disability.

statements.appliesTo: students awarded an honours degree in osteopathy
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown understanding of what is distinctive about osteopathic treatment, so as to work well with other health professions when needed and secure the best outcomes for patients and populations.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will understand osteopathy's distinctive approach well enough to collaborate effectively with other professions for the best patient and population outcomes.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold, you will understand what makes osteopathy distinctive, so you can work well with other health professions for the best results for patients and communities.

statements.appliesTo: students awarded an honours degree in osteopathy
statements.about: knowing the limits of one's own competence
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown awareness of the limits of their own competence, skill, knowledge and experience in practice, education and research, and will seek development through CPD, mentoring and shadowing or refer the patient to another osteopath or health professional as fitting.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will know the limits of their competence across practice, education and research and respond by seeking CPD, mentoring or shadowing, or by referring on.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold, you will know the limits of your own skills, knowledge and experience, and respond by seeking more training, mentoring or shadowing, or by referring the patient to someone better placed.

statements.appliesTo: students awarded an honours degree in osteopathy
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown understanding of, and commitment to, continuing self-directed professional learning that shapes practice, tracks and improves the quality of care and uses current advice and research.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will show commitment to ongoing self-directed professional learning that informs practice, monitors and improves care quality and draws on current advice and research.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold, you will be committed to directing your own learning throughout your career, using current advice and research to keep improving the care you give.

statements.appliesTo: students awarded an honours degree in osteopathy
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown awareness and effective use of clinically relevant research, clinical experience and patient expectations to support and judge evidence-informed practice critically, for the development of practice standards and patients' care.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will apply relevant research, clinical experience and patient expectations to support and critically evaluate evidence-informed practice.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold, you will combine research, clinical experience and what patients expect to judge and improve the care you give, critically and on good evidence.

statements.appliesTo: students awarded an honours degree in osteopathy
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown understanding and the ability to judge critically their own professional integrity, with attention to probity, respect, self-care and the duty of candour in practice.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will critically evaluate their own professional integrity, attending to probity, respect, self-care and the duty of candour.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold, you will be able to judge your own professional integrity critically, paying attention to honesty, respect, looking after yourself and being open when things go wrong.

statements.appliesTo: students awarded an honours degree in osteopathy
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown they can make decisions in unfamiliar, complex and unpredictable professional settings, using leadership, resilience, commitment and accountability.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will make decisions in unfamiliar, complex and unpredictable professional settings, showing leadership, resilience, commitment and accountability.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold, you will be able to make decisions in situations that are new, complex or unpredictable, showing leadership, resilience, commitment and accountability.
